messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall-sre: High p95 latency oscillation detected for smart-routing (latency-slo) across US regions. Trigger rate: 18 events/min. Auto-fallbacks detected. Please respond.

maya: i'm on it. i've started looking at the routing dashboard — p95 in us-west jumped from ~420ms to 1.8s and systems are flipping routes every ~90s. seems like the SLO trigger is too aggressive.

andrew: taking pager. assigning to me for mitigation + comms. maya — can you dump the last 10m of routing decisions?

maya: pasted recent window (simplified):
```
[00:00] route: us-west -> model: gptx-8k-q8 (latency 1.9s) p95 > 750ms => trigger reroute
[00:01] route: us-east -> model: gptx-8k-q4 (latency 420ms)
[00:02] route: us-west -> model: gptx-8k-q8 (latency 2.1s) p95 > 750ms => reroute
[00:03] route: eu-central -> model: gptx-8k-q8 (latency 2.0s)
[00:04] route: us-east -> model: gptx-8k-q4 (latency 430ms)
```
Notes: routing policy currently: smart -> prefer lowest p95 under 750ms, fallback uses model_variant priority list [gptx-8k-q8, gptx-8k-q4, gptx-8k-q2]. That priority is wrong. It picks q8 first which is slower for our current kernel path.

paul: that model_variant order is definitely backward. q8 is a high-precision variant that triggers slower kernels on A100s for long sequences. someone must have pushed that policy change last night.

olivia: i see a policy update at 1782467000 by eng-runtime (PR #2419) — commit message: "adjust fallback priority to prefer higher quality variants". looks like they inverted priority inadvertently.

andrew: ok quick plan: 1) stop the oscillation by disabling latency-triggered reroutes (set routing.policy.latency.enabled = false) 2) revert/patch the fallback ordering to prefer q4 then q8 3) roll out canary for 10% then 100% 4) postmortem to follow. any objections?

sarah: +1. recommended mitigation: change trigger window to use p99 or raise threshold to 2s instead of full disable to avoid masking real regressions. but since customers are affected and routes are flapping, immediate disable looks reasonable for now.

maya: impact: customers hitting interactive chat in us-west see jitter and token-generation stalls; no data loss. estimated affected requests: ~8% of global traffic, errors none but elevated tail latency. severity P2.

andrew: i'm going to make the temporary change now. executing API call: 
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/v1/routing/policy/latency -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -d '{"enabled": false, "reason":"mitigate oscillation"}'
```

deploy-bot: config-change: POST /api/v1/routing/policy/latency by andrew — status: accepted, revision: r_2026_178250_12

deploy-bot: config-apply: routing.policy.latency.enabled set to false in prod (all regions) — applied in 8s

andrew: flipping fallback order next. applying patch: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/routing/policy/fallback
payload: { "model_variant_priority": ["gptx-8k-q4","gptx-8k-q8","gptx-8k-q2"], "reason":"correct inadvertent inversion" }
```

deploy-bot: config-change: PATCH /api/v1/routing/policy/fallback by andrew — status: accepted, revision: r_2026_178250_13

deploy-bot: config-apply: fallback priority updated (us-west, us-east, eu-central) — propagated in 12s

maya: monitoring: p95 in us-west dropped from ~1.9s -> 480ms within 90s of the change. reroute chatter disappeared. looks stable so far.

paul: good. follow-up: schedule a canary of latency-triggered reroute with new priority and more conservative threshold: set threshold to 2s and window to 5m, or use p99 99th instead of p95. also add a cooldown so routes cannot flip more than once per 10m.

andrew: agreed. i'll open a short-lived feature flag for latency routing with cooldown and p99 gating. doing canary at 10% for 30m.

andrew: can someone notify impacted customers and set status page?

sarah: i'm drafting the status update. noting scope: "tail latency increase for realtime chat in us-west; mitigation deployed; stable; working on guarded re-enable." will publish in 10m after we confirm stability.

maya: quick root cause notes: 1) config change inverted fallback priority 2) policy used p95 with an aggressive threshold and no cooldown 3) model variant q8 interacts poorly with current kernel selection for typical prompt lengths, causing high latency — route planner saw high p95 and bounced traffic, which then pushed load into other regions and caused cascade.

olivia: filing incident ticket and tagging eng-runtime + eng-platform for follow-ups (PR need: revert + add integration test to ensure priority semantics, add simulated kernel-latency tests).

andrew: timeline for post-incident: immediate mitigation done. next steps: (a) roll out guarded latency routing canary with p99 + cooldown (b) revert bad policy PR and replace with controlled change + unit tests (c) postmortem within 48h with action items.

maya: +1. i'll keep monitoring for 60m then handoff to on-call rotation.

andrew: handing off: i'm off at 19:00UTC, leaving follow-up to sarah on communications and maya on monitoring. if any regression, page oncall-sre again.

sarah: ack. will watch alerts. thanks team. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: incident-note: temporary config r_2026_178250_12 and r_2026_178250_13 applied.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. severity: P2. responder: andrew.

andrew: quick notes for pager handoff: metric to watch -> routing.p95.us-west and routing.flip_count; action -> if flips > 3 within 10m re-disable latency routing and page.

maya: leaving live dump links here: https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/routing?from=1782509999&to=1782510800 and logs: https://logs.redwood/q=route_id:xyz-17825

paul: thanks. will add follow-ups to eng-runtime backlog.

olivia: creating postmortem stub now. tagging oncall and eng-runtime.

andrew: closing here. will update thread if anything else pops.

incident-bot: closed at 1782510800 (mitigated -> monitoring).
